text: A Cargo-installed papercuts binary was absent from PATH even though Cargo itself was available; invoking papercuts by name failed. A repository wrapper that also checks the Cargo bin directory would have prevented it.

note: Root cause: Cargo binaries were installed under CARGO_HOME/bin while that directory was not on PATH. Durable fix: scripts/papercuts prefers PATH, falls back to the Cargo bin directory, and enforces v0.2.0. Verified with ./scripts/papercuts --version and ./scripts/papercuts doctor.

text: papercuts 0.2.0 list --status all --format md marks resolved entries but omits resolution.note, hiding the reusable solution. Searching the pretty JSON output would have exposed the resolution.

note: Root cause: the v0.2.0 Markdown renderer does not include resolution.note. Workaround: use ./scripts/papercuts --pretty list --status all when searching prior problems and solutions. Verified that the JSON item includes status and the complete resolution object.

text: analyze-via-sonar skill: token 'vigilant-local-analysis' existed but its value was persisted nowhere (.claude/sonar.env held only SONAR_ADMIN_PASSWORD), so generate failed with 'already exists' and the run needed revoke+regen, silently invalidating a possibly live token. Persisting SONAR_TOKEN in .claude/sonar.env and reusing it would have prevented this.

note: Root cause: skill step 2 never persisted the generated token. Durable fix: SKILL.md step 2 now reads SONAR_TOKEN from .claude/sonar.env first (validates via GET /api/system/status, 200 = reuse), falls back to revoke+generate, and appends the fresh token to .claude/sonar.env (gitignored). Current token already stored. Verified: git check-ignore .claude/sonar.env -> IGNORED.

text: Full ./gradlew build (with JaCoCo+detekt overhead) failed once in BypassProxyServiceTest 'proxies method path query headers body and response' with UnprocessedRequestException/SessionProtocolNegotiationException: connection established, but session creation timed out (gateway WebClient.of() -> test upstream). Plain ./gradlew test and isolated rerun of the same suite passed. Library-default WebClient has no explicit timeouts/pooling - exactly the VIG-05-05 gap. Recording until VIG-05-05 lands explicit client config; recheck flake rate after it.

Read-only Codex CLI smoke with codex exec --ephemeral emitted a stale models-cache error (missing base_instructions), remote plugin-catalog 429/500 warning, and repeated state-db discrepancy warnings before a successful answer. The warnings bury the behavioral result; a cache repair path or quieter graceful fallback would have prevented this.

Metrics E2E tests read OTel data immediately after client response aggregation, but MetricsService publishes completion metrics asynchronously from RequestLog.whenComplete; full-suite timing exposed a missing-metric race that isolated runs hid. A shared deadline-bounded metric await helper prevents this flake.

note: Root cause: RequestLog completion callbacks may publish metrics after client aggregation completes, so direct reads raced. Durable fix: MetricsServiceTest.awaitMetric polls the OTel reader with a 5-second deadline for completion metrics. Verified: ./gradlew test --tests 'io.vigilant.gateway.metrics.*' passed all 8 tests.

text: Verification pipeline could report PASS with report-only OWASP and stale or empty Sonar scope

note: Fail-closed OWASP threshold preflight; explicit Sonar scope, async-task polling, project-key check, infrastructure exit code, and bounded Docker preflight

text: OtlpMetricsExportTest flaked in full suite (404 on /v1/models, single-run green): ServerSocket(0).use{localPort} reserved a port from the OS ephemeral range - the same pool fixture servers bind via http(0), so a fixture could steal it before the child JVM bound. Prevented by reserving the child port from below the ephemeral range and holding ServerSocket until launch.

note: Root cause: port TOCTOU between test JVM and child gateway JVM over the shared ephemeral pool. Fix: reserveGatewayPort() in OtlpMetricsExportTest binds a verified port in 1024..49151 (below macOS ephemeral range 49152+) so fixture http(0) servers cannot be handed it. Verification: ./gradlew test --tests io.vigilant.gateway.metrics.OtlpMetricsExportTest plus full ./gradlew test green.

text: RTK wrapper rejects find compound predicates even though global instructions require prefixing every shell command with rtk; using rg --files for repository inventory avoids the unsupported syntax.

note: RTK find intentionally rejects compound predicates. Durable repository-inventory workaround: use rtk rg --files with include/exclude globs. Verified against the full tracked file inventory for this review.

text: Concurrent Gradle builds can corrupt build/test-results when a yielded exec session is mistaken for completion; preserve and poll the session id before starting another Gradle command.

note: Root cause: a yielded exec session id was discarded and a second Gradle build started before the first had definitely completed, racing over build/test-results. Durable workflow: retain the session id, poll it to exit, and use one --no-daemon verification build. Verified by ./gradlew build --no-daemon completing GREEN in 3m 33s.

text: Official SWIFT IBAN registry downloads were reachable through the browser/web fetcher but stalled with zero bytes through shell curl, so direct artifact ingestion could not be used; documenting a supported source-fetch path or checked-in provenance generation script would prevent rediscovery.

note: Shell curl remained unusable for swift.com, but the official release 102 PDF was accessible through the web fetcher. Verified source version, all 89 country codes, and uncertain/new lengths from the PDF, then pinned them in a provenance-headed resource covered by IbanCountryLengthsTest. Reuse the web PDF path when direct download stalls.

text: prepareRedMadRobotPiiCorpus created its temporary download target before Files.copy but omitted REPLACE_EXISTING, so the explicit network path failed with FileAlreadyExistsException; use replacement copy into the owned temp file.

note: Root cause: Files.createTempFile makes the target exist, while Files.copy(InputStream, Path) rejects an existing target by default. Added StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING for the owned temp target. Verified: ./gradlew prepareRedMadRobotPiiCorpus downloaded, checked, and published the pinned file successfully.

text: Sonar analysis completed successfully but printed 'File Comparisons.kt not found in project sources'; a documented cause or scanner exclusion would prevent recurring unexplained noise.
RTK's filtered curl/jq output corrupted SonarQube API JSON captured between commands and caused jq parse failure; use 'rtk proxy curl' and 'rtk proxy jq' for machine-readable API pipelines.

note: Root cause: RTK output filtering is unsafe for JSON captured between curl and jq. Durable workaround: use 'rtk proxy curl' and 'rtk proxy jq' for SonarQube API pipelines, then validate every raw response with jq -e. Verified by fetching quality gate, measures, all issues, hotspots, rule details, and server status for the successful analysis task.

text: RTK-filtered Gradle output reported compileKotlin UP-TO-DATE after a Kotlin source edit even though the resulting class file timestamp proved compilation occurred; use 'rtk proxy ./gradlew' when task execution state is verification evidence.

note: Root cause: RTK's Gradle formatter can summarize task states in a way that is unsuitable as execution evidence. Durable workaround: run verification builds as 'rtk proxy ./gradlew ...'; add --rerun-tasks when forced recompilation is required. Verified by a narrow run showing all 7 tasks executed and BUILD SUCCESSFUL, followed by a raw full build GREEN.

text: RTK-filtered find output stripped directory components before xargs wc, causing valid generated corpus paths to be treated as missing basenames; use rtk rg --files or rtk proxy find for machine-consumed path pipelines.

note: Root cause: RTK's find formatter is presentation-oriented and removes path components, so its output is unsafe as xargs input. Durable workaround: use 'rtk rg --files <directory>' for inventories or 'rtk proxy find' when exact paths are required. Verified by counting all generated corpus files with an rg --files pipeline.

text: Full-suite load can make BypassProxyStreamingTest observe the first client callback after the upstream's final chunk even though the SSE variant passes and a forced focused rerun of both streaming tests is green; replace the cross-thread timestamp race with explicit synchronization that proves delivery before releasing the final chunk.

Detector test latch fired inside detect() before DetectorExecutionCoordinator published the returned result, so advancing a manual deadline raced and misclassified the supposedly completed detector as unfinished; completion-sensitive fixtures need an observation after result publication.

note: Root cause: a latch inside Detector.detect() proves only that the return path started, not that SharedDetectorExecution published the result to policy consumers. Durable fixture approach: capture the per-task virtual thread and join it with a bounded timeout before advancing manual policy time. Verified by the focused mixed detected/deadline test passing.

text: PERF-01 packaged gateway fixture no longer starts after mandatory politics.conf was introduced because PerfProcesses does not provide VIGILANT_POLITICS_CONFIG; perfTest exits before load with gateway exit code 2

note: Root cause: PerfProcesses launched packaged MainKt without the mandatory policy config added by EPIC-04. Durable fix: set VIGILANT_POLITICS_CONFIG to the repository's validated politics.conf.example in the benchmark-only child environment. Verified by a 20 RPS perfTest smoke completing all direct/proxy populations with zero failures.

text: EPIC-09 completion criteria require a project work-item validator, but the repository has no Gradle task, script, or CI step that implements or names one; provide the validator command beside the criterion or wire it into build.

BypassProxyServiceTest deadUpstreamUri released an OS-ephemeral ServerSocket(0) port before the gateway connected; under the full suite another Armeria http(0) fixture could occupy it, producing an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM instead of the expected 502. Reserving dead endpoints outside the OS ephemeral range would prevent this port-TOCTOU flake.

note: Root cause: deadUpstreamUri released an OS-ephemeral port before the gateway connected, allowing concurrent http(0) fixtures to bind it. Durable fix: select and validate a non-ephemeral port outside the fixture allocation range. Verified by the full BypassProxyServiceTest and scripts/pipeline-verify completing GREEN.

text: Full ./gradlew build intermittently makes BypassProxyServiceTest upstream failure logging case receive HTTP/2 RST_STREAM INTERNAL_ERROR even though the gateway emits the expected upstream_unavailable event; the exact method passes in isolation and in its focused class, so full-suite load still exposes an unresolved stable-error race or shared-client fixture leak

note: Added ./gradlew validateWorkItems with fixture coverage for registry, epic, issue, status, progress, membership, backlink, and Done-checklist drift; wired it into check. Verified by workItemValidatorTest, validateWorkItems, and ./gradlew build.

text: perfTest delegates to generic gatlingRun without pinning PerfLoadSimulation; after InspectionLoadSimulation was added the non-interactive Gradle task prompts for a simulation and fails with No line found

note: Root cause: perfTest depended on generic gatlingRun after the source set gained a second simulation, so Gatling required interactive selection. Durable fix: pin gatlingRun to io.vigilant.perf.PerfLoadSimulation and set non-interactive single-simulation execution. Verified by a packaged perfTest smoke completing direct and proxy phases with 12/12 successful requests.

text: Logback 1.5 does not substitute properties in the appender class attribute, so parameterizing production and slow-sink ConsoleAppender classes in one shared include fails configuration; share only identical async topology and protect sink/encoder equivalence with a runtime contract test

note: Root cause: Logback model processing does not resolve variables in appender class names. Durable approach: keep sink declarations explicit, share the identical bounded AsyncAppender through logback-async-stdout.xml, and compare production/slow topology and JSON encoder at runtime. Verified by LoggingConfigurationEquivalenceTest and LoggingConfigurationTest.

text: Resolved detector-deadline fixture race recurred: the test again advances manual time after a latch inside Detector.detect(), before SharedDetectorExecution publishes the completed result; restore a bounded post-task-completion barrier and protect it from regression

note: Root cause: the detector-return latch fired before SharedDetectorExecution published the normalized result, so manual deadline advancement raced under full-suite load. Durable fix: awaitPublishedDetectorResult bounded-joins the captured per-task virtual thread before advancing manual time. Verified by the focused deadline test and scripts/pipeline-verify full build plus verifyAll.
